content: Vic Mensa is one of those people who has done so many things that it’s hard to remember where you were first introduced to him. Was it his debut mixtape Innanetape, which finally hit the major streaming services for the first time in September? Or maybe his house-influenced single “Down On My Luck”? Maybe you didn’t even realize that Mensa was a rapper. Maybe you know him from his roles on The Chi or Bel-Air. Or perhaps you’re mostly aware of him through his activism, social media presence (peeling oranges and waxing poetic), or his podcast The Vic Mensa Show. Point is, the man wears many hats. Part of the secret to being so prolific, it turns out, is Voice Memos. Just capture those ideas before they disappear. What is your most indispensable tool? Voice Memos. Everything starts there for me. Songs, essay ideas, orange tree thoughts, voice notes to myself at some wild hour, little things my son says that I do not want to lose. My phone is a million distractions in one rectangle, but Voice Memos is one of the few parts of it that still feels honest. Just press record before the thought disappears. Which social media platform do you use the most? Instagram, for better or worse. That’s definitely where my voice has really found its legs. I started out peeling an orange and talking through whatever was on my mind, and it turned into this whole conversation with people about politics, history, music, grief, jokes, fatherhood, all of it. That response helped show me there was room for The Vic Mensa Show too. Instagram can be a circus, obviously, but it’s also a very valuable tool for connection. Which tech trend do you wish would go away? Maybe Meta glasses. Them motherfuckers seem like they’re being used for evil. What creation are you most proud of? Probably my upcoming album right now. It’s the first album that I’ve really taken myself completely seriously as a producer. The surrounding art, videos, design, clothing, and world I’m building around it is something that really excites me as well. What do you do when you need to focus? I either do my Shambhavi Mahamudra meditation that I learned from Sadhguru or the Wim Hof breathing method. Ideally, I’ll do the Wim Hof breathing method in the steam room and then the meditation. What do you think is worth splurging on? Anything that touches your life every day. A good mattress. Good headphones. Quality food. Clothes you will actually keep for years. Experiences with your child. I have wasted money on plenty of dumb shit, so I am trying to be better about buying things that either last or make a real memory. What would the tagline for your biopic be? Live from the contradiction. What is the last GIF or meme you used? [Image: Ummm… that is not Vic Mensa. Also, the letter casing here is pure chaos. https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/10/unnamed_2e795d.jpg?quality=90&strip=all]

chineseContent: 维克·门萨（Vic Mensa）是做过如此多事情的人之一，以至于很难记住你是在哪里第一次被介绍认识他的。这是他的首张混音带 Innanetape，最终于 9 月份首次登陆主要流媒体服务吗？或者也许是他受浩室影响的单曲“Down On My Luck”？也许你甚至没有意识到门萨是一位说唱歌手。也许您是通过他在《The Chi》或《Bel-Air》中的角色认识他的。或者，也许您主要是通过他的激进主义、社交媒体形象（剥橘子和充满诗意）或他的播客 The Vic Mensa Show 来了解他。重点是，这个人身兼多职。事实证明，如此多产的秘诀之一就是语音备忘录。在这些想法消失之前抓住它们。你最不可或缺的工具是什么？语音备忘录。对我来说一切都从那里开始。歌曲、散文创意、橙树的想法、在某个狂野时刻给自己的语音笔记，以及我儿子说的我不想失去的小事。我的手机在一个矩形中包含一百万个干扰因素，但语音备忘录是它的少数几个仍然感觉诚实的部分之一。在这个想法消失之前按下录音键即可。您最常使用哪个社交媒体平台？ Instagram，无论好坏。这绝对是我的声音真正发挥作用的地方。我开始剥一个橘子，畅所欲言，然后就变成了与人们谈论政治、历史、音乐、悲伤、笑话、父亲身份等等所有的话题。这个回应让我知道维克门萨秀也有空间。显然，Instagram 可以是一个马戏团，但它也是一个非常有价值的联系工具。您希望哪种技术趋势消失？也许是元眼镜。这些混蛋看起来像是被用来作恶的。您最引以为傲的创作是什么？可能是我即将发行的专辑
